subject: SLO validation: harness transfer + artifact ownership
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLO validation: harness transfer + artifact ownership

Hi Ellie — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned for the performance validation: 

Summary of BrightCart targets (from discussion)
- 95th pctl latency target: <= 120ms for short prompts (~32 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: 600 requests/minute with typical prompt mix (see prompt bucket below)
- Concurrency target: support 80 concurrent RPS from your edge region during peak flash sales
- Streaming requirements: token-level flush within 20ms and total start-of-stream latency < 80ms for streaming chat sessions

What Redwood will deliver this week
- Prompt set v1 (attached): representative seeds + labeling for short/medium/long buckets
- Measurement spec draft (attached): exact metric definitions, windowing, stereo sample sizes
- Harness instructions markdown (attached): how to run the reproducibility harness against our hosted test endpoint or your test cluster

Action items / owners
1) Redwood: share the full prompt CSV, harness instructions, and a minimal test dataset by EOD Wed (LOGAN)
2) BrightCart: confirm which model family to validate against (open-weight vs quantized) and whether we can provision a short-lived ingress token for streaming playback (ELLIE)
3) Redwood engineering: map prompt buckets to recommended model/quantization profile and produce a quick-cost estimate for the measured run (BEN)
4) Both: schedule a 60-minute bench run on Tue next week (preferred) — tentative Wed/Wed options included in the Drive folder link below (LOGAN + MARISSA)

Notes on reproducibility and scope
- Our measurement_spec defines a two-pass approach: dry-run (functionality check) then structured run (statistical sample). We’ll publish the harness command that pins seeds, sequence lengths, and KV cache warm-up.
- For streaming, the harness will exercise a playback mode that matches your client chunk sizes; we need your client chunk-size config or we’ll default to 64-token chunks.

Attachments: prompt_sets_v1.csv, harness_instructions_v0.3.md, measurement_spec_draft.pdf
Drive (shared workspace): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBrightCartPromptSet

If that all looks right, please confirm model family and whether procurement needs an NDA before we upload any PII-adjacent examples. Happy to tighten the prompt set if you prefer synthetic-only examples.

Thanks,
Logan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
O: +1 415-555-0192

---
(attachment stubs)
- prompt_sets_v1.csv (55 KB)
- harness_instructions_v0.3.md (4 KB)
- measurement_spec_draft.pdf (120 KB)

From: Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@brightcart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO validation: harness transfer + artifact ownership

Thanks, Logan — clear summary and helpful artifacts. A few clarifying items before we proceed: 

1) Model family: we want you to validate against an open LLaMA-family variant first (4096 context) then a quantized runtime if the delta is >15% on latency. Procurement would like the cost delta documented.
2) Ingress token: procurement will approve a scoped token limited to test IPs; I’ll confirm the allowed IPs by EOD Wed.
3) Streaming chunk size: our client typically uses 64-token chunks for chat, but we have a fallback 32-token chunk for low-bandwidth sessions. Please make both available in the harness.
4) Data: we prefer synthetic prompt examples for the initial run — we’ll provide a small holdout of anonymized real prompts if you need later for fidelity checks.

Next meeting: Tue 31 May 2027 at 10:00 PT works for our engineering lead. Can you send a calendar invite?

Best,
Ellie Ramos
Head of Product Engineering, BrightCart
ellie.ramos@brightcart.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLO validation: harness transfer + artifact ownership

Couple of engineering notes for the run planning: 

- Model mapping: for the LLaMA-family seed we should recommend two server variants: 1) fp16 on A10-class for latency baseline, 2) int8-quant avx-fused for cost baseline. I’ll sketch a quick bench matrix and attach a one-pager.
- Prompt bucketing: the CSV looks good but we should add a "long tail" bucket for 512+ tokens — even if rare, it can blow up latency percentiles. I’ll annotate the prompt_sets_v1.csv and return a prompt_sets_v1b.csv.
- Streaming test harness: we need a small end-to-end example showing how to open a chunked websocket, send chunk reservation headers, and measure per-token emission time. I put a harness snippet in harness_patch.diff (attached stub).

Action items for us: Ben -> produce bench matrix and prompt annotations by Thu EOD; Marissa -> confirm availability of a dedicated test slot on Redwood Dedicated for Tue 31 May (slot reserved or not)

Forwarding this to Ellie as well: hearing from procurement that the ingress token + IP list is the only gating item before we provision a scoped test endpoint.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLO validation: harness transfer + artifact ownership

Ellie — we tentatively have a Redwood Dedicated slot for Tue 31 May 10:00 PT but I need procurement to confirm the IP allowlist so we can attach the scoped ingress. If procurement delays, we can fall back to a hosted ephemeral endpoint but that will change the network latency characteristics (we'll flag that in the run notes).

For the streaming playback: here is the minimal client snippet we will use to measure per-token emission (included inline so you can validate):

--- begin snippet ---
# pseudo-code: open websocket, send input, read frames, timestamp
ws = WebSocketClient(url="wss://test.redwood.ai/stream?token=XXX")
ws.send(json.dumps({"prompt_id": "p-001", "chunk_size": 64}))
start = time.monotonic()
for frame in ws:
    ts = time.monotonic()
    emit_latency_ms = (ts - start) * 1000
    log_emit(prompt_id, frame.token_index, emit_latency_ms)
--- end snippet ---

If procurement can confirm the IP list today, Logan can provision the token and Ben can start warming the KV cache using the prompt_sets_v1b. Otherwise we should run a dry-run on Friday to validate harness correctness only (no SLA claims).

Marissa
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Referenced attachments: bench_matrix_onepager.pdf, prompt_sets_v1b.csv)

From: Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@brightcart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO validation: harness transfer + artifact ownership

Thanks all — procurement confirmed the test IP range (range: 34.120.0.0/14) and I uploaded a sanitized holdout of ~200 prompts to the Drive folder (file: brightcart_holdout_anonymized.csv). I also added a short checklist in the Drive doc titled "BrightCart - SLO validation checklist" with the items we agreed.

Short checklist highlights for Redwood: 
- Run dry-run and confirm harness reproduces deterministic latencies (pin seeds)
- Run structured measurement at 6M tokens or until 95% CI on 95th pctl <= 5% relative error
- Capture per-token emission timestamps for streaming and include raw trace logs (redacted) in the artifact bundle

We’re comfortable with synthetic prompts first; we’ll release a tiny real holdout if you need to reproduce fidelity. Go ahead and send the calendar invite for Tue 31 May 10:00 PT and provision the ingress token scoped to 34.120.0.0/14.

Ellie
